title: Testing & Quality
summary: Tests turn "I think it works" into "I know it works" — the safety net that lets you change code fast without fear.

blocks.markdown:
A test runs your code with a known input and asserts the output is what you expected.

- A **suite** of these is a **safety net** — it re-checks behavior in seconds after every change.
- The real value isn't catching a bug once; it's **fearless refactoring**: green suite means behavior preserved.
- **Quality is the byproduct.** Confidence to change code fast is the goal.
- The forcing function is **change** — software is edited for years, and every edit risks a **regression**.

blocks.subTitle: Which test for which job
blocks.markdown:
Match the test to the risk you actually fear.

| Situation | Reach for |
|---|---|
| One function's logic, no I/O | Unit test |
| Code talks through a real DB | Integration test |
| Critical user journey | One E2E test |
| Rule holds for any input | Property test |
| Two services agree on JSON | Contract test |

blocks.subTitle: Anatomy of a test (AAA)
blocks.markdown:
Almost every test follows **Arrange–Act–Assert**.

- **Arrange** — build a known starting state.
- **Act** — do exactly *one* operation.
- **Assert** — check one observable outcome.

A test with three Act steps and five asserts is doing too much — it's hard to debug when it fails. Keep it to **one logical behavior** so a failure points to one cause.

blocks.subTitle: The test pyramid
blocks.markdown:
The most important model in testing: shape your test *counts* like a pyramid.

![Many fast unit tests at the base, fewer integration, few slow end-to-end at the top](assets/d04-testing-quality/test-pyramid.svg)

- **Unit** base — many tests, ~1 ms each, no I/O.
- **Integration** middle — fewer, ~50–200 ms, touch a real DB or module.
- **E2E** top — a handful, seconds each, drive the whole system.
- A unit failure pins the broken function; an E2E failure could be anything. Aim for roughly **70/20/10**.

assets.alt: Many fast unit tests at the base, fewer integration, few slow end-to-end at the top

blocks.subTitle: A good unit test (FIRST)
blocks.markdown:
A solid unit test is **FIRST**.

- **Fast** — milliseconds, so a huge suite finishes in under a minute.
- **Isolated** — no real DB, network, clock, or other tests; runs alone, any order.
- **Repeatable** — same result every run; no `now()`, no randomness, no shared state.
- **Self-validating** — asserts pass/fail itself; you never read output by eye.
- **Timely** — written close to the code.

Plus the **one reason to fail** rule: test a single behavior.

blocks.subTitle: Test doubles
blocks.markdown:
To keep a unit isolated, replace real dependencies with stand-ins — **test doubles**.

![Spectrum of test doubles from dummy to mock, increasing in smartness](assets/d04-testing-quality/test-doubles-spectrum.svg)

- **Dummy** — fills a required argument; never used.
- **Stub** — returns canned answers; feeds state in.
- **Spy** — a stub that also records how it was called.
- **Fake** — a real but simplified impl, e.g. an in-memory DB.
- **Mock** — pre-set with expectations; fails the test if they aren't met.

assets.alt: Spectrum of test doubles from dummy to mock, increasing in smartness

blocks.subTitle: TDD: red–green–refactor
blocks.markdown:
Test-Driven Development writes the test *before* the code.

![TDD loop: red failing test, green make it pass, refactor while green](assets/d04-testing-quality/tdd-cycle.svg)

- **Red** — write a small test for behavior that doesn't exist; watch it fail (proves it tests something).
- **Green** — write the *simplest* code that passes, even if ugly.
- **Refactor** — clean up with the green net guarding you; then loop.

It forces interface-first design and testable code; feels slow on exploratory work.

assets.alt: TDD loop: red failing test, green make it pass, refactor while green

blocks.subTitle: Property-based testing
blocks.markdown:
Instead of hand-picking examples, state a rule that holds for *all* inputs.

```python
# property: encode then decode is identity
for any string s:
    assert decode(encode(s)) == s
```

- The tool throws hundreds of random inputs — empty, huge, unicode, emoji.
- On failure it **shrinks** to the smallest reproducing case, e.g. `"\0"`.
- Best for clear invariants: round-trips, sorting, idempotency, commutativity.

blocks.subTitle: Stub vs mock
blocks.markdown:
Both are doubles, but they test different things.

| Aspect | Stub | Mock |
|---|---|---|
| Tests | State | Interaction |
| Provides | Canned data | Expectations |
| Fails when | Outcome wrong | Call not as set |

A stub lets you assert "balance is 70"; a mock asserts "`charge()` called once." Over-mocking couples tests to *how* code works, so refactors break them — prefer asserting outcomes; mock only when the interaction *is* the guarantee.

blocks.subTitle: Picking the level
blocks.markdown:
You can't maximize speed and realism — choose by where the risk lives.

- **Pure logic** (input → output) → unit test; cheapest confidence there is.
- **Seam with a DB or queue** → integration test with a real or fake dependency. Mocking the DB hides the exact bug you fear.
- **Whole-app journey** → exactly one E2E for the happy path.
- **Cross-service JSON shape** → contract test, not slow multi-service E2E ([b16-monolith-microservices](b16-monolith-microservices.md)).

blocks.subTitle: Integration & contract testing
blocks.markdown:
These catch what unit tests can't.

- **Integration test** — your code plus a real Postgres in Docker. Catches a wrong SQL query, serialization mismatch, or bad connection config.
- **Contract test** (e.g. Pact) — the consumer records what it expects from a provider's API; the provider runs that contract in CI.
- If the provider drops a needed field, **its build goes red before deploy** — without ever running both services together. Cross-service safety at unit-test speed.

blocks.subTitle: Real systems & signals
blocks.markdown:
How teams run this at scale, and what they watch.

- **Google** — small/medium/large taxonomy; leans hard on tiny hermetic tests across a monorepo with tens of thousands of daily commits.
- **Netflix** — Chaos Monkey kills live instances to test resilience in production.
- **SQLite** — over 600× more test code than library code, fuzz plus property generation.
- **Watch:** suite runtime, flaky-test rate, escaped-defect rate, and coverage *trend* on new code.

The mistakes that bite in interviews and production:

- **"100% coverage = well-tested."** Coverage counts lines *run*, not asserted. Use **mutation testing** for a real quality signal.
- **Mock everything.** Couples tests to implementation; a behavior-preserving refactor breaks dozens.
- **"Flaky tests are fine, just retry."** Retrying hides real races and erodes trust in every red build.
- **"E2E is most valuable because it's realistic."** Slow and flaky — a thin top layer, not the foundation.
- **Time/randomness in logic.** Inject a clock/RNG; never call `now()` inside the code under test.
